official_statement_rationale: The headline CPI inflation at 7.44 per cent, significantly exceeding the upper tolerance band, is a matter of serious concern. While the surge is largely attributable to transitory supply-side shocks in food items, the persistence of these pressures could potentially unanchor inflation expectations if not addressed with vigilance. The robust GVA growth of 7.80 per cent provides us the space to prioritize price stability as our primary nominal anchor. I am of the view that a status quo on the policy repo rate is appropriate at this juncture to allow for a calibrated assessment of the incoming data, particularly the trajectory of food prices. However, given the excess liquidity of 120,000 crore in the banking system and the necessity to bring inflation back to the 4.00 per cent target, it is imperative to maintain the 'withdrawal of accommodation' stance. This approach ensures that our monetary policy remains focused on durable disinflation while supporting the ongoing growth recovery.
